claims.text: KARL WOLFE. Printed at section 3.8.4 under 'Testimony of Sergeant Karl Wolfe, US Air Force / September 2000'. Its editorial header: 'Karl Wolfe was in the Air Force for 4 1/2 years beginning in January 1964. He had a top secret crypto clearance and worked with the tactical air command at Langley AFB in Virginia. While working at a NSA facility he was shown photographs taken by the Lunar Orbiter of the moon that showed detailed artificial structures. These photos were taken prior to the Apollo landing in 1969.' In his own words: 'So I was asked to go over to this facility on Langley Air Force Base, where the NSA was bringing in the information from the lunar orbiter.'

claims.source: NASA NSSDCA master catalogue, spacecraft record for Lunar Orbiter 1 (1966-073A), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-073A , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE INSTITUTIONAL DISCREPANCY IN THE WOLFE ACCOUNT, FROM NASA'S OWN CATALOGUE. The NSSDCA record for Lunar Orbiter 1 states: 'The Lunar Orbiter program was managed by NASA Langley Research Center', a NASA civil facility at Hampton, Virginia, which is a separate installation from Langley Air Force Base. The same record gives launch on 10 August 1966 and photographic data acquired 'from August 18 to 29, 1966'.

claims.text: A CORRECTION THIS BOARD MAKES AGAINST ITS OWN SIDE OF THE ARGUMENT. The objection commonly made to Wolfe, that he dated the episode to 1965 when no Lunar Orbiter had flown, DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS DOCUMENT AND IS NOT ASSERTED HERE. The Briefing Document gives no year for the episode. It gives a service window of January 1964 plus four and a half years, which runs to about mid-1968 and therefore encloses the Lunar Orbiter photographic period of August 1966 to August 1967. Anyone wishing to make the chronology objection must first open the later Wolfe source in which he gave that date. This board did not open one.

claims.text: Karl R. Wolfe died on 10 October 2018, born 19 April 1944, per his funeral home obituary at Lansing, New York. A NEGATIVE WORTH RECORDING: the obituary does not mention US Air Force service, an employer, an education or a career.

claims.text: DONNA HARE. Printed at section 3.8.4 under 'Testimony of Donna Hare / November 2000'. Her heading carries no rank, service or agency, which is unusual in this document; the editorial header supplies it: 'Donna Hare had a secret clearance while working for NASA contractor, Philco Ford.' In her own words: 'During 70 and 71 I worked in Building 8 of NASA for a contractor, Philco Ford', and of the technician she describes, 'he said, well, we always have to airbrush them out before we sell them to the public.'

claims.source: Ford Motor Company corporate history, 'Ford, Philco and the Mission Control Center', https://corporate.ford.com/articles/history/ford-philco-and-the-mission-control-center.html , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE EMPLOYER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE EMPLOYEE IS NOT. Ford Motor Company's own corporate history records that Ford purchased Philco in 1961 and 'transferred its Aeronutronic Division to a new entity it called Philco-Ford'; that 'In 1963, the company went head-to-head against tech giants like IBM, RCA, Lockheed, Hughes Aircraft and AT&T in a bid to implement the Mission Control Center at the new Manned Space Center in Houston'; and that it was renamed Ford Aerospace and Communications Corporation in 1976 and sold to Loral in 1990.

claims.text: STATED INFERENCE ON HARE. By her own account in the same testimony she kept no copy of the image, does not name the technician, and gives no date beyond 'during the 70's, I don't know the exact date'. Her testimony also relays at second and third hand an unnamed man who was 'in quarantine with the astronauts' and an unnamed security guard made to burn photographs. THOSE ARE RELAYED CLAIMS AND MUST NEVER BE WRITTEN ON THIS BOARD AS ANYTHING ELSE.

claims.text: DON PHILLIPS. Printed at section 3.8.4 under 'Testimony of Mr. Don Phillips, Lockheed Skunkworks, USAF, and CIA Contractor / December 2000'. The editorial header states that he 'worked with Kelly Johnson at the Lockheed Skunkworks on design and construction of the U-2 and the SR-71 Blackbird'. In his own words the sighting was at 'Angels Peak... a classified radar installation', 'in 1966, to 67', with estimated speeds of '3,800 to 4,200 miles per hour equivalent, ground speed', and one named corroborating witness, 'a buddy that was chief radar operator named Anthony Kasar'.

claims.text: STATED INFERENCE ON PHILLIPS. NOTHING INDEPENDENT WAS FOUND: no personnel record, no Lockheed document, no CIA record, no USAF record, no publication by him, no contemporaneous report of the Angels Peak sighting, and no trace of the named corroborating witness. The name is extremely common. He is held in this set rather than given a node precisely so that an unverified claimant does not acquire edges into Tier A contractor nodes.

claims.text: JOHN WEYGANDT, AND THE NAME DISCREPANCY THIS BOARD MUST NOT REPEAT. The Briefing Document prints the heading 'Testimony of Lance Corporal John Weygandt / October 2000' at section 3.8.4. THE MODERN LITERATURE AND THE CANON-GAP AUDIT BOTH CALL HIM JONATHAN. No node should be created under a given name that this cluster's own primary source contradicts. His own printed account is unusually specific and is the obvious next test: enlisted under the delayed entry programme in July 1994 while still in high school, boot camp from 18 June, graduated 8 September 1995, MOS 0311, reassigned in late January 1996 to MOS 7212 Stinger Avenger, in training February to late May 1996, then Second Marine Air Wing, 28th Marine Air Control Group, second air defence battalion, Battery B from June 1996, transferred to 'the section for laser strike' in February 1997.

conflicts: Karl Wolfe places the Lunar Orbiter imagery at an NSA facility on Langley Air Force Base; NASA's own catalogue states the programme was managed by NASA Langley Research Center, a separate civil installation. The board carries the discrepancy of institution and does not resolve it.

The Briefing Document prints 'John Weygandt'; the surrounding literature and the canon-gap audit say 'Jonathan'. The board carries the source's spelling and records the conflict rather than picking a side.

desc: THIS IS A SET NODE AND NOT AN ORGANISATION; NOTHING HERE EVER MET AS A BODY. It exists because a person node built on one testimony in one interested-party document would assert that somebody said something and nothing else, and because sixty-eight of those would make `witness-chain` the dominant edge type of an entire region of this board, which CLAUDE.md section 6 warns turns degree into a measure of how much is claimed rather than of what is true. The set carries the roster and the counts, and individual witnesses are promoted out of it only when an independent record is found, which in this pass happened for John Callahan, Clifford Stone, Robert Jacobs and Larry Warren and did not happen for Karl Wolfe, Donna Hare, Don Phillips or John Weygandt. Those four are held here with their claims and with the specific documentary problems each carries: Wolfe's NSA-at-Langley account against NASA's own record that the Lunar Orbiter programme was run by NASA Langley Research Center; Hare's employer documented by Ford Motor Company while her employment is documented nowhere; Phillips with nothing independent at all; and Weygandt, whose name the Briefing Document prints as John while the modern literature calls him Jonathan, which is precisely the class of error this board keeps having to undo.
